lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Caring for Home and Shared Spaces
lessonRef.title: Application or project: hazard recognition

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice hazard recognition. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: A trusted adult walks the shared spaces of the home with the learner, and together they look specifically for hazards — not general messiness — such as a cord across a walkway, an unstable stack of items, a blocked doorway, or a sharp edge at a height where someone could bump it.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult must be present for the entire walk-through.
The learner does not touch, move, or attempt to fix any hazard without the adult's direction.
Stop and ask the adult for help immediately if the walk-through turns up broken glass, exposed wiring, or anything unfamiliar or unclear.

simulationAlternative.description: If a full walk-through of two shared spaces isn't possible, the learner instead reviews four printed or hand-drawn room scenes with their adult, identifies the hazard in each one, names its category, and proposes a fix — reviewed and confirmed by the adult the same way as the real walk-through.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Which confirmed hazard surprised you the most — something you wouldn't have noticed on your own before this lesson? What made it easy to miss?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Hazard identification accuracy: Adult confirms at least four real hazards across two categories. | Category naming and proposed fixes: Names the correct category and proposes a workable fix for each confirmed hazard. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner do a hazard walk-through of one space outside the home they visit regularly (with an adult), such as a relative's house, and compare which categories of hazard showed up there versus at home.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can practice hazard recognition. I will do one step at a time and check one result.

duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

resources.title: hazard recognition worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: A trusted adult walks the shared spaces of the home with the learner, and together they look specifically for hazards — not general messiness — such as a cord across a walkway, an unstable stack of items, a blocked doorway, or a sharp edge at a height where someone could bump it.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact hazard recognition decision or action.
Model move 2: Before the walk-through, list two hazard categories you already know to look for (for example: trip risk, sharp edge, blocked exit, unsecured heavy object).
Model move 3: With your adult present for the entire walk-through, look at two shared spaces together and point out anything you think might be a hazard.

Model check: Hazard identification accuracy: Adult confirms at least four real hazards across two categories. | Category naming and proposed fixes: Names the correct category and proposes a workable fix for each confirmed hazard.

resources.title: hazard recognition action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for hazard recognition.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: hazard recognition coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A trusted adult walks the shared spaces of the home with the learner, and together they look specifically for hazards — not general messiness — such as a cord across a walkway, an unstable stack of items, a blocked doorway, or a sharp edge at a height where someone could bump it.
Coach direction: Before the walk-through, list two hazard categories you already know to look for (for example: trip risk, sharp edge, blocked exit, unsecured heavy object).
Learner prompt: Name two hazard categories.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: hazard recognition complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult present for the entire walk-through, look at two shared spaces together and point out anything you think might be a hazard.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I found at least four things to check, not just one.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My adult confirmed which findings were real hazards and which were not.
Response 3 (t2-p3): For every hazard my adult confirmed, I could name which category it fit (trip, sharp edge, blocked exit, unsecured object, other).
Response 4 (t2-p4): I did not touch or try to fix anything without checking with my adult first.

Equal-access rule: If a full walk-through of two shared spaces isn't possible, the learner instead reviews four printed or hand-drawn room scenes with their adult, identifies the hazard in each one, names its category, and proposes a fix — reviewed and confirmed by the adult the same way as the real walk-through.

resources.title: hazard recognition minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which confirmed hazard surprised you the most — something you wouldn't have noticed on your own before this lesson? What made it easy to miss?

Success checks: Hazard identification accuracy: Adult confirms at least four real hazards across two categories. | Category naming and proposed fixes: Names the correct category and proposes a workable fix for each confirmed hazard.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: hazard recognition supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional hazard recognition condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Hazard identification accuracy: Adult confirms at least four real hazards across two categories. | Category naming and proposed fixes: Names the correct category and proposes a workable fix for each confirmed hazard..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

realRoute.title: hazard recognition — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Do not begin the physical action until a household-authorized guardian gives permission and is available for the supervision or review named in this lesson.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
With your adult present for the entire walk-through, look at two shared spaces together and point out anything you think might be a hazard.

simulationRoute.title: hazard recognition — complete fictional route

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Which confirmed hazard surprised you the most — something you wouldn't have noticed on your own before this lesson? What made it easy to miss?

Category naming and proposed fixes: Names the correct category and proposes a workable fix for each confirmed hazard.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Hazard identification accuracy: Adult confirms at least four real hazards across two categories. | Category naming and proposed fixes: Names the correct category and proposes a workable fix for each confirmed hazard.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
